transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... I've been having these nights where I just eat. And afterwards, I'll just sit there with all these crumbs and empty containers around me, and I feel so ashamed. I get so disgusted with myself that I can hardly even pray, or look folks at church in the eye the next morning. That's what brought me in.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever feel the need to do something to get rid of the food or compensate for the calories, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?
No, I don't do anything like that. I just... sit there with it. I don't try to throw up or take anything, and I certainly don't exercise. I just feel awful about it and carry on.
During these times when you eat this way, do you feel like you are unable to stop or are unable to control how much you are eating?

Yes, I do. Once I take that first bite... well, usually after the house is quiet for the night... it's like my good sense just steps aside. Even while I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now,' my hands just keep reaching for more. I really just can't seem to stop myself once I start.
